title: Listen to the warnings
description:
This program works, yet the compiler has three warnings about it (look at the **Problems** tab after pressing Run). Warnings are the compiler saying "this is legal, but are you sure?" and they are right more often than not.

Change the code so that it builds with **no warnings** and still prints `7` for the input `7.9`.
hints: Two of the warnings are about variables that are defined and never used. Delete them.
The third is about squeezing a `double` into an `int`, which silently loses the decimals. If that is what you want, say so: `static_cast<int>(measured)`.
rules: The compiler must report no warnings.
lessonTitle: Compiler Settings, Build Configurations and Undefined Behavior
